name: The Royal Forest
firstVisit: The trees close in behind you. Every way looks the same.
Somebody has carved something into that tree.

T: Old trees, packed close. Every one of them looks like the last one.
g: Long grass. Nobody's trodden it down in a long time.
k: A gap in the undergrowth, just wide enough for a boy.
o: A gap in the undergrowth, just wide enough for a boy.
>: East: back out to the South Road.
1: Scratched into the bark, small and careful: a sparrow, every feather there. It's flying north.
2: A horse, cut quick and deep into the trunk. It gallops south.
The legs are wrong. He didn't stop to fix them.
3: A boy, running. Fewer lines now, cut hard. He runs west, straight on.
Behind him the bark's been scored over and over, until it's nearly black.
4: Not a picture any more. Gouges. Eyes, all down the trunk, dozens of them.
And through the eyes, one clean arrow, pointing north. Cut with whatever nerve he had left.
5: A sparrow, half done. One wing, and the start of the other.
z: Dead grass, in a ring. Nothing's grown here in a long, long time.
The rest of the clearing is green right up to its edge, and not a blade over.
u: The husk of an old cocoon, split down the middle and gone grey, half sunk into the earth.
Whoever was in it left a long time ago.
w: A woodpile, stacked neat. Every log from the first row of trees. None from the second.
^: A path north between the oaks, lined with white roses gone half wild.

objects.name: Woodcutter
lines: I cut at the edge. I don't go in.
Nobody goes in. Not if they want to come out the same day they went.

answer: Paths in there don't stay put. You walk in straight and you walk out where you started, scratching your head.
My gran said a prince ran in there once, five hundred years back, and the forest shut behind him.
My gran said a lot of things. I still don't cut past the first row.
Folk say somebody drew the way. On the trees.
Follow the pictures. Not your nose. Your nose'll walk you in circles.

questions.ask: A woodcutter, scared of trees. Brave.
answer: Aye. Says the one about to walk into them.
* He goes back to his chopping. He chops a bit harder.
